title: Grade 3 Social-Emotional Learning & Civics
description: Empathy, emotional regulation, inclusion, active listening, and civic responsibility.

items.prompt: During recess, you notice a new student standing alone watching others play tag. How can you show active inclusion?

options.text: Walk over, introduce yourself, and invite them to join the game
Point and whisper with your friends
Ignore them and keep playing
Tell them the playground is full

items.explanation: Inviting isolated peers into group activities demonstrates empathy and inclusive leadership.

items.prompt: When you feel overwhelmed or frustrated during a challenging test, what is a healthy self-regulation strategy?

options.text: Rip up the test paper in anger
Take three deep breaths, pause, and focus on one question at a time
Yell across the classroom
Lay your head down and refuse to try

items.explanation: Deep breathing and cognitive pausing help calm the nervous system to regain focus.

items.prompt: What does it mean to be an 'upstander' instead of a 'bystander' when you witness bullying?

options.text: Standing quietly and filming with a phone
Joining in with the teasing
Safely speaking up to support the person and telling a trusted adult
Cheering on the bully

items.explanation: Upstanders actively intervene safely and seek adult support to protect vulnerable peers.

items.prompt: What is an essential component of active listening when someone is speaking to you?

options.text: Looking at your shoes and playing with a toy
Talking over the person
Thinking about lunch while they talk
Maintaining eye contact, nodding, and not interrupting

items.explanation: Active listening requires attentive posture, eye contact, and respectful patience.

items.prompt: Why are democratic community rules and classroom constitutions important?

options.text: They keep everyone safe, ensure fairness, and help learning thrive
They exist only to give punishments
To prevent children from having any fun
They have no real purpose

items.explanation: Community rules establish physical safety, mutual respect, and an orderly learning environment.

items.prompt: If you make a promise to clean your pet's cage every Saturday, keeping that promise demonstrates:

options.text: Carelessness
Impulsiveness
Accountability and dependability
Greed

items.explanation: Following through on commitments demonstrates reliability and responsible pet ownership.

items.prompt: What is an example of showing respect for diverse family structures and backgrounds?

options.text: Judging families that look different from yours
Appreciating that every family has unique traditions and loving caregivers
Telling someone their traditions are wrong
Ignoring cultural heritage months

items.explanation: Respecting diversity means valuing each individual's unique family background and identity.

items.prompt: How can children participate in civic service in their local neighborhood?

options.text: Leaving empty soda cans in public parks
Writing on neighborhood walls
Staying indoors all year
Volunteering to plant trees or donate canned goods to a food pantry

items.explanation: Community volunteerism builds strong civic engagement and improves shared public spaces.

items.prompt: When two friends want to play with the same swing at recess, what is the fairest solution?

options.text: Take turns using a timer so both enjoy equal swing time
Push the other person off the swing
Whoever is taller gets to keep it the whole recess
Break the swing

items.explanation: Turn-taking and equitable sharing resolve playground resource conflicts fairly.

items.prompt: What does having a 'Growth Mindset' mean when learning something difficult?

options.text: Believing you are either born smart or not
Quitting immediately when you make a mistake
Believing your brain can grow stronger with effort, practice, and perseverance
Never asking for help

items.explanation: A growth mindset recognizes that cognitive abilities develop through effort, feedback, and practice.
